svg.title: Spark Cash Plus Spend Ladder
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-spark-cash-plus-spend-ladder; chapter number: 6; title: Spark Cash Plus Spend Ladder; subtitle: Where the flat 2 percent charge card pays, from $1M framing down to a single award seat; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Every $1 Million Spent; value: 1000000; display: $1,000,000; conversion: $20,000 back at 2%; detail: Ryan Maya runs inventory, software and Facebook ads through the card and reports over $50,000 in cash back over a few years.; label: Annual Fee Refund Threshold; value: 150000; display: $150,000; conversion: $150 fee credited back; detail: Capital One credits the annual fee once yearly spend reaches $150,000 (Bytes Media).; label: Beats No-Fee 1.5% Cards; value: 30000; display: $30,000; conversion: Both net $450; detail: Above about $30,000 a year the 2% card minus its fee beats 1.5% no-fee cards (Ask Sebby Business).; label: Break-Even on the Fee; value: 7500; display: $7,500; conversion: 2% covers $150; detail: Solved $150 = 2% times spend for the break-even line (Ask Sebby Business).; label: Cash Back Shared Into Miles; value: 1320; display: $1,320; conversion: 132,000 miles, ~$8,500 seat; detail: Spark cash back moved into Capital One miles, then 130,000 Singapore miles for a JFK to Singapore saver award (Ask Sebby Business).; caption: Spark Cash Plus is a no-preset-limit charge card paying a flat 2% that must be cleared every month; the highest-leverage exit converts cash back into partner miles.; assumptions note: Spark products pull all three personal bureaus and report to personal credit, which affects Chase 5/24 math (Just Money Ish, HowToCredit); a 2.99% late fee applies to unpaid statement balances (Bytes Media).; note: Sources - Ask Sebby Business, Bytes Media, Ryan Maya, Just Money Ish, HowToCredit.

rect.title: label: Every $1 Million Spent; value: 1000000; display: $1,000,000; conversion: $20,000 back at 2%; detail: Ryan Maya runs inventory, software and Facebook ads through the card and reports over $50,000 in cash back over a few years.
label: Annual Fee Refund Threshold; value: 150000; display: $150,000; conversion: $150 fee credited back; detail: Capital One credits the annual fee once yearly spend reaches $150,000 (Bytes Media).
label: Beats No-Fee 1.5% Cards; value: 30000; display: $30,000; conversion: Both net $450; detail: Above about $30,000 a year the 2% card minus its fee beats 1.5% no-fee cards (Ask Sebby Business).
label: Break-Even on the Fee; value: 7500; display: $7,500; conversion: 2% covers $150; detail: Solved $150 = 2% times spend for the break-even line (Ask Sebby Business).

label: Cash Back Shared Into Miles; value: 1320; display: $1,320; conversion: 132,000 miles, ~$8,500 seat; detail: Spark cash back moved into Capital One miles, then 130,000 Singapore miles for a JFK to Singapore saver award (Ask Sebby Business).

text.title: Assumptions: Spark products pull all three personal bureaus and report to personal credit, which affects Chase 5/24 math (Just Money Ish, HowToCredit); a 2.99% late fee applies to unpaid statement balances (Bytes Media).
